crop_profile.summary: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is an annual fruit crop thriving in warm, humid climates with 18-30°C temperatures, 60-80% humidity, and 500-1000 mm annual rainfall. It prefers loam soils, pH 5.5-7.0, good drainage, and high nitrogen. Drip irrigation, balanced NPK (10-10-10) and organic amendments boost yields of 60-90 t/ha. Major producers include China, India, USA, Turkey, and Egypt. Key challenges are late blight, early blight, Fusarium wilt, and pests like fruit worm, whitefly, and aphids. Proper irrigation, fertilization, timely harvest, and refrigerated storage ensure high-quality marketable fruit.

recommendation.justification: Satellite imagery shows critically low NDVI and high NDWI, indicating severe water stress and poor photosynthetic activity. High humidity raises disease risk, so prompt irrigation will also help reduce leaf wetness duration. Apply a thin layer of organic mulch (e.g., straw or compost) around the tomato rows to conserve moisture and reduce soil exposure.
Inspect plants for early signs of fungal disease (blight, wilt) during irrigation cycles.
Record irrigation volumes and timing in a farm log.

Adjust irrigation frequency based on moisture readings and NDVI trends.

Activate drip irrigation to deliver 20‑30 mm of water per week, applying in 2‑3 day intervals.
Apply a thin layer of organic mulch (e.g., straw or compost) around the tomato rows to conserve moisture and reduce soil exposure.
Inspect plants for early signs of fungal disease (blight, wilt) during irrigation cycles.
Record irrigation volumes and timing in a farm log.
steps.justification: Satellite imagery shows critically low NDVI and high NDWI, indicating severe water stress and poor photosynthetic activity. Soil assessment reports adequate nitrogen but low organic carbon, increasing the need for moisture to support nutrient uptake. High humidity raises disease risk, so prompt irrigation will also help reduce leaf wetness duration. Temperature and wind are optimal, providing a window to recover yield potential before fruit set is compromised.
steps.influence: Translated the executive decision into concrete recommended actions.
